You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point and lowers the points of every other member by 0.3. In the same way, every token another member keeps in their own account lowers your points by 0.3.
- Each token in the group account pays you 0.3 points and does not change any other member's points.
- Every round, every member also receives 18 points, whatever anyone does.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game with negative externalities: keeping a token privately yields 1 point to me but costs each of the other 3 members 0.3 (a total externality of -0.9), while putting it in the group account gives only 0.3 to me and has no effect on others. So from a purely individual standpoint, private contributions dominate, but they impose a larger collective cost than the group alternative.

Socially, keeping a token private nets +0.1 overall, whereas putting it in the group yields +0.3 overall, making cooperation the better choice for total welfare even though private contribution is individually dominant regardless of what others do. So the rational self-interested play across all 10 rounds would be to contribute nothing to the group, though this conflicts with the socially optimal outcome where everyone cooperates.
